children: Oman’s Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning (MoHUP) has received seven bids for a major road and infrastructure construction package under Phase 1 of Sultan Haitham City.

Najed Al Ahliya submitted the lowest bid at 117.92 million Omani rials ($306.59 million), while The Arab Contractors Oman Limited submitted the highest at OMR169.51 million ($440.72 million), according to tender opening results.

Other bidders were Galfar Engineering and Contracting at OMR121.78 million ($316.62 million), Al Tasnim Enterprises at OMR129.46 million ($336.59 million), Strabag Oman at OMR135.76 million ($352.98 million), Sarooj Construction Company at OMR137.25 million ($356.86 million) and United Gulf Construction Company Oman Branch at OMR162.29 million ($421.95 million).

The tender, titled “Phase 01, WP16 – Construction of Transport Network Connectivities from Sultan Qaboos Road, and Associated Extension of Roads, Infrastructure and Utilities,” was issued on 13 March 2026.
Bids were originally due on 28 April, with opening scheduled for 29 April. The bid submission and opening timelines were subsequently extended to 2 September 2026.

The scope covers external road links connecting Sultan Haitham City to Sultan Qaboos Road, together with bridges, flyovers, underpasses and utility buildings. It also includes stormwater drainage systems, culverts, wadi channels and medium- and low-voltage electrical installations.
he works are intended to strengthen connectivity, support utilities integration and ensure the effective functioning of the city’s primary road network.
(Writing by Deva Palanisamy; Editing by Anoop Menon)
